newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Security exercises spark APEC bomb scares.
newsitem.headline: Security exercises spark APEC bomb scares.

text.p: "No threats to APEC seen", the Manila Chronicle proclaimed on Thursday as security exercises sparked bomb scares at the city's international airport and the Subic Bay site for the APEC summit.
Manila is suffering from security jitters as ministers and officials from around the Pacific Rim gather for the 18-member Asian-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
The head of the Philippines' national organising committee for the six-day gathering, retired General Lisandro Ababia, defused the bomb scare after a night of confusion.

"It's very clear now it was just an exercise," he told Reuters of the scares on Wednesday at Subic, the huge former U.S. naval base northwest of Manila where the APEC leaders will meet next Monday, and at the capital's Ninoy Aquino international airport.
The government has mobilised a 27,000-member army of security personnel for the meetings of officials and ministers in Manila and the leaders at Subic.

Security guards with U.S.-trained bomb sniffer dogs have enveloped Manila's seafront convention centre. More than 2,000 journalists covering the conference were carefully quarantined from the main area where foreign and economic ministers representing half of the world's peoples were meeting.
The government has banned carrying of guns in Manila for the duration of the conference, apparently a major hardship in a country whose love affair with firearms rivals that of the United States.

The ban prompted a howl of outrage from Philippine Daily Inquirer columnist Ramon Tulfo, in a city where newspaper advertisements offer handguns and assault weapons on credit and night clubs ask you to check knives and guns at the door.
"Must the government impose that stupid ban on the carrying of firearms for citizens whose lives are in danger just to assure the safety of our guests?" he demanded.
"Why is the government so paranoid that the safety of law-abiding citizens has to be put at stake by denying them the privilege to carry guns far from the summit venue?"
Adding to government paranoia has been vociferous opposition from a variety of groups and organisations to the APEC meeting.
Organisers moved two delegations -- from Papua New Guinea and Hong Kong -- out of a midtown hotel on Thursday when it was realised an anti-APEC forum was due to be held there.
